what: In a folder that is not a git repository, the comment count lists nothing and reports "0 comments in 0 files", however many comments the files hold. This will matter at ticket 06. The proof program checks each deliberate break in a plain copy of the tracked files, with no git history, so the planned break that adds a comment would pass the patterns check and the proof would report it as not caught. The same is true of the starter kit unpacked from a download. Separately, a new file that has not yet been added to git is not counted either. I ran it: a copy made the way prove.py makes its copies, holding a Python comment, came back with no comments listed. The cause is that comment_hits asks `git ls-files` for its list of files and ignores the error git gives outside a repository, so a failure reads as a clean folder. Ticket 05 will copy this pattern when it moves the function into the patterns check. Fixing it now is one change; fixing it later means one change per ticket that reuses it.
